open_obligations: Note that the result is correlational.
Check that the 15 tasks are drawn from Burns et al.'s 22 NLP datasets.
Check the effect with alternative similarity metrics, which Goel et al. say also hold.
out.other_title: Open questions on understanding weak-to-strong generalization and salience
out.rationale: Burns et al. ask how different kinds of weak label errors affect generalisation. Goel et al. report that, controlling for the accuracy gap, weak-strong similarity is inversely correlated with weak-to-strong gain (r = -0.35, p < 0.01), so less correlated errors give larger gains; models are 1-3B weak and 7-9B strong, not GPT-4-family.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how the kind of weak-label errors affects weak-to-strong gains, for 12 weak-strong pairs on 15 NLP tasks

text: After partial correlation controlling for the accuracy gap between weak supervisor and strong student, the paper reports that similarity remains inversely correlated with weak-to-strong gain (r = -0.35, p < 0.01), so tasks where supervisor and student make less correlated errors tend to yield larger improvements; the authors say the trend also holds with alternative similarity metrics.
title: Weak-to-strong gain is larger when weak supervisor and strong student are less similar
